title: Exact Accepted Bottom-Interface Exchange Result Transport
reason: Current canonical can rerun SWAP transactionally from the same checkpoint, and the serialized reference backend already accounts the exact per-trial bottom contribution as bottom_flux * accepted step duration, but trial_outcome_t, transaction_result_t, canonical_result_t and kernel_result_t do not publish that contribution separately. F-GC21 therefore cannot stage the F-GC19R-R1 mass ledger from an exact accepted whole-window SWAP interface exchange without either forbidden reconstruction from aggregate mass totals or an invalid terminal-flux-times-window approximation.

scope.goal: Transport the already-accounted accepted bottom-interface exchange and accepted terminal bottom flux as explicit model-native result data, preserving accepted-route provenance across retries, full/two-half temporal qualification and model-certificate qualification.

required_semantics: A rejected full trial, rejected half trial, failed retry or rolled-back attempt must never contribute to the published interface exchange.
For TX_ROUTE_TWO_HALF, accepted bottom exchange is exactly the sum of half1 and half2 accepted bottom exchanges; terminal bottom flux is the accepted half2 terminal value.
For TX_ROUTE_MODEL_CERTIFIED, accepted bottom exchange and terminal bottom flux come only from the accepted certified outcome.
Across canonical internal accepted substeps, exact bottom exchange is accumulated only from accepted transaction results; terminal flux comes from the final accepted substep.
A non-completed canonical interval must not publish a whole-window exchange as available.
Kernel candidate/result transport must preserve the exact accepted result without exposing HeadCalc or solver-private arrays.
The transaction/canonical/kernel result stays in model-native depth and flux units. Unit conversion to the groundwater contract remains an explicit runtime/coupler responsibility through F-GC17.
No inference from canonical total_in/total_out and no terminal_flux * whole_window approximation is allowed.
Existing hard mass accounting is unchanged and remains independently checkable against the separated bottom contribution.
